title: Rav Yechezkel (father of Rav Yehuda)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a leading figure and a man of good deeds in Shmuel’s time. He had two distinguished sons, Rami and Rav Yehuda. Hyman says Yehuda surpassed his father in Torah, as shown in [Kiddushin 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32a.9-13): when Rav Yechezkel taught Rami the mishnah about those sentenced to burning mixed with those sentenced to stoning, Yehuda said, “Father, do not teach it that way.” Shmuel, Yehuda’s teacher, told him to address his father differently. Hyman cites 33a for the report that even Mar Shmuel rose before Rav Yechezkel, because he was a man of good deeds. Shmuel therefore told Yehuda to rise before his father. In [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.9.2.21) and [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.1.3.4), “R. … bar Yechezkel” reports his father’s blessing for rain: “May Your name, our King, be magnified, sanctified, blessed and exalted for every drop You send us.”[^1]
In [Berakhot 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.11a.19), Rav Yechezkel taught, “One who acted according to Beit Shammai has acted validly,” and so on.

notes.text: Both Jerusalem Talmud passages give the reporter’s full name as Rav Yehuda bar Yechezkel. The wording supplied for Hyman gives only an abbreviated reporter. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2046&lang=en) places the instruction to stand at [Kiddushin 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.33b.5), as does Davidson. Heilprin describes Yehuda as his father’s teacher.
